title: Molecular Extraction Lab: Caffeine & Oleic Acid Synthesis
description: The user operates a virtual chemistry extraction lab where a coffee mat represents a caffeine source and an avocado represents an oleic acid source. The user must perform a multi-step solvent extraction procedure by dragging each specimen into a reaction vessel, adjusting temperature and solvent ratio sliders, initiating extraction cycles, and combining the two extracts to synthesize a novel compound, with each parameter validated against correct chemistry ranges.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive molecular extraction lab. Load both GLB assets using GLTFLoader: coffeemat.glb (placed on the left bench area, scale ~2.0) and Avocado.glb (placed on the right bench area, scale ~8.0). Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 6) looking at origin, with OrbitControls limited to prevent going below the bench. Add ambient light (0.5 intensity) and two directional lights simulating lab overhead fluorescents. Create a flat plane as a lab bench surface with a subtle grid texture. In the center, place a translucent cylindrical mesh (glass reaction vessel) with MeshPhysicalMaterial (transmission 0.7, roughness 0.1). Implement these interaction steps with validation: Step 1: Click-and-drag the coffeemat into the vessel (raycasting detection, must land within vessel bounds). Step 2: A temperature slider appears in an HTML overlay panel; user must set it between 85-95°C (validate range, show error if outside). Step 3: A solvent concentration slider appears; user must set it between 60-80% ethanol (validate range). Step 4: Click an Extract button that triggers a 3-second animation where the vessel glows green and the coffeemat dissolves (scale to 0 with opacity fade). Step 5: Click-and-drag the Avocado into the vessel similarly. Step 6: A pH slider appears; user must set it between 6.5-7.5 (validate). Step 7: A pressure slider appears; user must set between 1.5-2.5 atm (validate). Step 8: Click a Combine button that triggers a synthesis animation where the vessel contents swirl (rotating particle system inside the vessel using Points with BufferGeometry), change color from green to golden, and a floating 3D text label appears above reading 'Caffeoyl-Oleate Ester — Synthesis Complete'. Track progress with a step indicator bar at the top of the screen. Each validated step enables the next. Use dat.gui or simple HTML controls for sliders.
